subject: general
question: An artificial leaf to create fuel from sunlight was developed by which Indian organisation?
solution:
The correct answer is __**CSIR.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **CSIR **is the **Council of Scientific and Industrial Research** - National Chemical Laboratory in Pune.
 
• The researchers at CSIR have developed an** artificial leaf.**
 
• The leaf absorbs sunlight to generate hydrogen fuel from water.
 
• It is an advance that may provide clean energy for powering eco-friendly cars in the future.
 
• The device consists of semiconductors stacked in a manner to simulate the natural leaf system.
 
• When visible light strikes the semiconductors, electrons move in one direction, producing electric current.
 
• The current almost instantaneously splits water into hydrogen.
 
• Researchers believe is one of the cleanest forms of fuel as its main by-product is water.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** Council of Scientific and Industrial Research** was established by the Government of India in **September 1942.**
 
• It is an autonomous body that has emerged as the largest research and development organization in India.
 
• It runs** 38 laboratories, 39 outreach centers, 3 Innovation Centres and 5 units **throughout the nation.
 
• It has a collective** staff of over 14,000**, including a total of 4,600 scientists and 8,000 technical and support personnel.
 
• It is mainly funded by the **Ministry of Science and Technology**.
 
• It operates as an autonomous body through the Societies **Registration Act, 1860.**
